title: The Cat's Paw Nebula
caption: The Cat's Paw Nebula, NGC 6334, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-meter telescope at La Silla
celestial: Cat's Paw Nebula, NGC 6334 · constellation Scorpius · about 5500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This portrait shows the Cat's Paw Nebula, NGC 6334, a vast star-forming region about 5500 light-years away in Scorpius. The whole gas cloud spans about 50 light-years, and it appears strongly red.

That red color has two causes. The red light comes mainly from hydrogen gas lit up by the fierce light of hot young stars. On top of that, the material between the nebula and Earth scatters and absorbs blue and green light more efficiently than red, much as dust and haze redden a sunset.

NGC 6334 ranks among our galaxy's busiest nurseries of massive stars and has been studied extensively. It hides freshly formed brilliant blue stars, each nearly ten times the Sun's mass and born within the last few million years. It is also home to many baby stars buried deep in dust, which makes them hard to study. Altogether, the Cat's Paw may hold several tens of thousands of stars.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (30.71 x 31.91 arcminutes) and distance (5500 light years), the frame spans roughly 49 × 51 light-years. Its light set out about 5,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image from the Wide Field Imager combines blue, green and red filters with a hydrogen filter. The caption explains that the red comes mostly from glowing hydrogen, but the full filter-to-color mapping is not published.
understand.eye: The long exposures gather far more light than the eye, so the nebula's red glow is much more vivid here than through a telescope eyepiece.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The picture was made with the Wide Field Imager on the 2.2-meter MPG/ESO telescope at La Silla in Chile, combining blue, green and red filters with a special filter that lets through the light of glowing hydrogen.
alt: A large, strongly red nebula of glowing gas and dark dust scattered with stars.
